title: Recommend and implement one small feature at a time
goal: Keep the requirements interview's implementation proposal small and actionable by recommending one independently verifiable next feature instead of asking the user to choose among oversized first-version bundles.
in_scope: Update the project-local requirements-interview skill to maintain a full feature map as a roadmap while separating it from the current implementation step.
Split broad end-to-end product flows into small, independently verifiable features before recommending implementation work.
Recommend one next feature at a time, using user value, independence, cross-cutting needs, and dependency order to explain the recommendation.
When a foundational capability such as login is required by user-specific data access, recommend that capability as a small prerequisite feature; do not treat login as universally mandatory.
List other features as later roadmap candidates instead of bundling them into large A/B MVP choices.

After the user chooses the next feature, complete and show only that feature's specification and wait for its explicit implementation approval; after it is implemented and verified, stop and discuss the next feature.
out_of_scope: Removing the full roadmap or dependency map from requirements artifacts.
Combining several independently verifiable features into one spec for convenience.
acceptance_criteria: The skill distinguishes the full roadmap from the one next feature proposed for implementation.
It recommends one small, independently verifiable feature and explains its prerequisites and rationale.
It avoids presenting oversized whole-product bundles as A/B first-version choices.
Remaining roadmap features are recorded as later candidates and are selected only after the current feature is complete and reported.
Login or another common capability is proposed first only when the confirmed requirements make it necessary or valuable as a prerequisite.
The per-feature specification and explicit approval gate remains in force.
